declared.name: nitrification
declared.note: Oxidises ammonium to nitrate. Requires oxygen, so it happens at oxic interfaces. Nitrate is not directly usable by most of this ecosystem — it must be reduced again, which is what makes the anaerobic pathway valuable.
declared.reason: Cannot close under POOL_COMPOSITION: NH4 and NO3 are single-element nitrogen carriers, so the oxidant draw has no product to reach; changing either carrier breaks denitrification (its only consumer would need ~15 C per 2 NO3 to shed the oxygen) or the sediment-release path (H manufactured from nothing). At chem/0.8.0 the pathway was kept live with its oxygen reduced to a presence gate while still earning energy; the Owner review of 2026-10-18 found that a material mechanism departure and accepted isolation as the fallback. Recorded in CHO-081-RESULTS.md and CHEM-080-CONTRACT.md.
